# acre&key Answers (answers.acrenkey.com)

> Comprehensive, legally verified due diligence knowledge base for residential flat buyers in Bengaluru (Karnataka, India). Published by acre&key (Acrenkey Realty LLP), an independent Home Buyer Concierge firm and registered Karnataka RERA real estate agent (PRM/KA/RERA/1251/446/AG/260814/007659).

## About acre&key Answers

## RERA Compliance & Builder Diligence

- [How do I tell whether a property ad is RERA-compliant?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/advertisement-rera-number-check/): Check three things. The project must be registered before it's advertised (section 3). The ad must prominently show the Karnataka RERA website address and the project's registration number (section 11(2)). And the number must match the project and phase on the portal. If you pay relying on a false ad, section 12 gives you a right to compensation. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [What counts as &#x27;affordable housing&#x27; for the 1% GST rate?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/affordable-housing-gst-1-percent-definition/): In Bengaluru, a flat is an "affordable residential apartment" for the 1% GST rate only if its carpet area is 60 sqm or less and the gross amount charged is ₹45 lakh or less. Gross amount includes land or undivided share, parking, preferential location and other promoter charges on top of the base price. Check with your CA. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [When must a builder hand over the apartment association and common areas in Karnataka?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/apartment-association-handover-karnataka/): The RERA Act makes the builder help form an association of allottees and, after the occupancy certificate, hand common areas and documents to it. If local law is silent, the association is due within three months of a majority of units being booked, and conveyance within three months of the OC. Get the handover list in writing. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [How does an investment consultant assess builder track record in Bangalore?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/assess-builder-track-record-bangalore/): A careful real estate investment consultant looks at what the builder has actually delivered, not what it advertises. That means past projects' promised vs actual completion dates, whether occupancy certificates were issued, complaints and orders on the Karnataka RERA portal, build quality and upkeep in finished projects, how residents' associations were handed over, and any signs of financial strain. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [How can I check a project on the Karnataka RERA website before buying?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/check-project-karnataka-rera-website/): Go to rera.karnataka.gov.in, use the project search to find the project by name or promoter, and open its registration details. Check that the registration is valid, the promoter and land match your documents, the approvals and sanctioned plans cover the tower and phase you're buying in, the declared completion date suits you, and there are no worrying complaints. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [Construction-linked vs time-linked payment plan: which is safer?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/construction-linked-vs-time-linked-payment-plan/): For most buyers, a construction-linked plan is safer, because you pay as the building actually goes up, so your money tracks real progress. A time-linked plan asks you to pay on fixed dates, whether or not construction has kept pace, which can leave you having paid a lot for a building that's behind. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [What documents should be verified before paying a token advance for a flat in Bangalore?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/documents-verify-before-token-advance-bangalore/): Before any token, check the project's Karnataka RERA registration and what the promoter filed there (approvals, commencement certificate, sanctioned plan, title declaration). Then check the title chain, Encumbrance Certificate, khata, land conversion where relevant, the draft agreement and the cost sheet. A consultant can gather these; a lawyer should give the title opinion. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [How do I file a complaint with Karnataka RERA?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/file-complaint-karnataka-rera-online/): Any aggrieved person, including an allottees' association, can complain to Karnataka RERA under Section 31 of the RERA Act. K-RERA's FAQ says complaints go in Form 'N' with a ₹1,000 fee. Compensation claims under Sections 12, 14, 18 and 19 go to an adjudicating officer, not the Authority. The Authority aims to decide within 60 days. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [Villa vs apartment in East Bengaluru: what actually changes?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/gated-villa-vs-apartment-east-bengaluru/): In the villa vs apartment choice, the real difference is what the deed gives you. An apartment gives you a unit plus an undivided share of the land. A villa may give you a marked plot, or just a bigger undivided share. Check that first, then compare land per rupee, upkeep per home and approvals. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [How do you gift a flat to a family member in Karnataka?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/gift-deed-flat-family-karnataka/): Gift deed stamp duty Karnataka charges for close family is fixed: ₹5,000 within BMRDA, BBMP or city corporation limits, ₹3,000 in municipal council or town panchayat areas, and ₹1,000 elsewhere, plus cess, surcharge and a registration fee. Gifts outside the family list pay the same duty as a sale. You register the deed on Kaveri. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [How much GST do I pay on a new flat, and when is it zero?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/gst-on-flat-purchase-rates/): GST on an under-construction flat bought from a builder is usually 1% without input tax credit for an affordable house and 5% without input tax credit for others, under the GST Council's 34th-meeting decisions. If the entire price is paid after the completion certificate or first occupation, whichever is earlier, this GST does not apply. Check invoices with a CA. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [Do I need home insurance for a new flat, and what does it cover?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/home-insurance-new-flat/): Home insurance for a flat is your choice, not a RERA requirement on buyers, but it fills gaps the builder's duties don't. IRDAI's standard home policy, Bharat Griha Raksha, covers your flat and its fittings, and optionally your contents, against fire, flood, earthquake, storm, riots and similar events. It does not pay for poor construction. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [What documents do you need to sell or buy an inherited flat?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/inherited-flat-sale-documents/): The core inherited property sale documents are the death certificate, the will or proof of who the heirs are, the parent deed and title chain, and the khata in the heirs' names. Every heir must sign the sale or release their share by a registered deed. Probate is no longer mandatory, but buyers and banks may still ask. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [Is GST charged on apartment maintenance in Bengaluru?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/maintenance-charges-gst-apartment/): CBIC Circular No. 109/28/2019-GST clarifies that RWA maintenance contributions up to ₹7,500 per month per member can be exempt. GST applies only when that monthly contribution exceeds ₹7,500 and the RWA's annual aggregate turnover is ₹20 lakh or more. If the monthly amount exceeds the limit, the circular taxes the entire amount, not only the excess. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [New launch or resale flat in the same area: what changes for me?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/new-launch-vs-resale-flat-what-changes/): A new launch is bought from a promoter, so the RERA Act's promoter duties, the 10% advance cap and construction GST come into play. A resale flat is bought from an owner, so title history, the OC, khata and the seller's paperwork carry more weight. Compare the risks as well as the price per square foot. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [Does a housing society nomination replace a will?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/nomination-vs-will-flat/): No. In the nomination vs will property question, the will decides who owns your flat; a nomination only tells a society, association or bank whom to deal with after your death. The Supreme Court has held that a nominee isn't the owner and heirs keep their rights. To leave the flat to someone specific, write a valid will. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [What does an NRI need to buy a flat in East Bangalore without travelling?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/nri-us-buy-bangalore-without-travel-poa/): You need four things: money routed through Indian banking channels (inward remittance or an NRE, FCNR(B) or NRO account), a trusted person in India holding your power of attorney, a Bangalore consultant who can run video visits and handle documents, and your own lawyer and CA. NRIs can buy flats, but not agricultural land or farmhouses. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [Can OCI cardholders buy flats in Bengaluru?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/oci-buy-property-india-rules/): Yes. The OCI property purchase India rules under FEMA match an NRI's: you can buy flats, houses, plots and commercial property without RBI approval, but not farmland, farmhouses or plantations. Pay through Indian banking channels or NRE, FCNR(B) or NRO accounts. A 2021 Supreme Court ruling didn't change this, the RBI says. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [Why does one project have several RERA registration numbers?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/phase-wise-rera-registration/): Because RERA treats each phase as its own project. The Explanation to section 3 says that where a project is developed in phases, every phase is a stand-alone real estate project needing separate registration. So a large township can carry several RERA numbers, each with its own completion date, approvals and quarterly updates. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [Can I claim home loan interest paid before possession?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/pre-construction-interest-deduction/): Yes, but not in the years you paid it. Section 22(1)(c) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 lets interest for the period before the tax year in which the home is acquired or constructed be claimed in five equal instalments, starting that year. For a self-occupied home, caps and your tax regime decide how much you actually get. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [Is it safe to pay an EOI for a pre-launch project in Bangalore before RERA registration?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/pre-launch-projects-bangalore-risk/): It's risky, and a real estate investment consultant shouldn't push you into it. Section 3 of the RERA Act says a promoter can't advertise, market, book, sell or offer for sale any unit in a project that needs registration until it's registered. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [How much do real estate consultancy services cost in Bangalore?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/real-estate-consultancy-services-cost-bangalore/): On new projects in Bangalore, real estate consultancy services often cost the buyer nothing directly, because the developer pays the consultant. On resale, you may pay a brokerage. Some advisers charge a fixed fee instead. There's no single official rate, so ask each firm for its exact terms in writing before you start. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [Rent vs buy in Bengaluru: how should you work it out?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/rent-vs-buy-bengaluru/): For rent vs buy in Bengaluru, compare a year's rent with a year's unrecoverable cost of owning: loan interest, maintenance, tax and the return your down payment could have earned. Add the one-time 7.6% stamp and registration charges. Buying wins if you'll stay long enough for price growth to cover the gap. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [Renting out a flat in Karnataka: agreement, stamp duty and police check](https://answers.acrenkey.com/rental-agreement-new-owner-karnataka/): Under rental agreement Karnataka rules, a home let for up to a year pays stamp duty of 0.5% on the rent and deposit, capped at ₹500. Longer leases pay 1% with no cap and must be registered. Tell the local police station about your tenant; the state's online tenant service was listed as under modification on 19 Oct 2026. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [My project&#x27;s RERA date was extended. What does it mean for me?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/rera-extension-what-it-means-buyer/): Section 6 lets the Authority extend a project's registration for force majeure, or in reasonable circumstances without promoter default, with written reasons, capped at one year in aggregate. An approved extension moves the registration end date. It does not by itself rewrite your agreement possession date or cancel section 18 delay rights. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [How do I read a project&#x27;s quarterly progress report on Karnataka RERA?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/rera-quarterly-progress-report-how-to-read/): Open the project on rera.karnataka.gov.in and look at four things the promoter must update every quarter: units booked, garages booked, approvals taken and pending, and construction status with photographs. Then check the dates. A page that hasn't moved in several quarters is a question to put to the builder in writing. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [What happens if my project&#x27;s RERA registration has lapsed?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/rera-registration-lapsed-project/): A RERA registration is valid only for the completion period the builder declared, plus any section 6 extension (capped at one year in aggregate for reasons other than force majeure). If it lapses or is revoked, section 8 lets the Authority, after consulting the appropriate Government, arrange the remaining work, including through the association of allottees. Section 18 protects you. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [What should I check on a site visit to an under-construction project?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/site-visit-checklist-under-construction/): Open the project's Karnataka RERA page before you go. At the site, match the RERA number on the board, ask to see the sanctioned plans, compare the build stage with the builder's last quarterly update, and treat the sample flat as a sales tool. Write down what the sales team says and get key answers in writing before paying. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [Do women get a stamp duty concession in Karnataka?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/stamp-duty-women-buyers-karnataka/): On stamp duty for female in Karnataka, the rates are the same as for men. The Stamp Act's conveyance rates don't vary by the buyer's gender, and we found no notification giving women a concession as of 19 Oct 2026. A flat above ₹45 lakh in Bengaluru costs about 7.6% in charges whoever's name is on the deed. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [Does RERA require title insurance, and does it protect me?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/title-insurance-rera/): Section 16 of the RERA Act requires the builder to obtain the insurances the appropriate Government notifies, including on the title of the land and building and on construction. The builder pays the premium, and the benefit passes to you when the agreement for sale is signed. It applies only once notified, and it doesn't replace your own title check. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [Can a real estate consultancy compare under-construction and ready-to-move flats for me?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/under-construction-vs-ready-to-move-consultancy/): Yes, and it's one of the more useful things real estate consultancy services can do. A side-by-side comparison should cover total cost, delay risk, GST, loan interest during construction, what you can inspect, the paperwork, and when you can actually live there or rent it out. The right answer depends on your timeline and how much risk you can carry. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [What is undivided share (UDS) of land, and why should a flat buyer care?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/undivided-share-uds-explained/): Undivided share is your proportionate interest in the land and other common areas of the project, held together with every other owner and never split off as a separate piece. Under RERA, the builder must convey that proportionate title in the common areas to the association, so check how your agreement and sale deed state it. (Author: Piyush Mittal)

## Agreements, Contracts & Possession

- [Allotment letter, agreement for sale, sale deed: what is the difference?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/allotment-letter-vs-agreement-vs-sale-deed/): An allotment letter is usually an early booking paper. The agreement for sale is the registered contract that fixes price, specifications and the possession date under RERA. The sale deed (conveyance) transfers title to you. Under section 13, a builder can't take more than 10% of the cost before that agreement is written and registered. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [Which booking form clauses should I check before paying for a flat?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/booking-form-clauses-red-flags/): Check how much the form asks you to pay, what happens to that money if you or the builder back out, and whether it binds you to terms you haven't seen. Under section 13 of the RERA Act, a promoter can't take more than 10% of the cost as an advance or application fee before a registered agreement for sale. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [Can a builder change the plan after I book a flat?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/builder-changes-plan-after-booking/): Not freely. Under section 14(2) of the RERA Act, once plans and specifications are disclosed to you, the builder needs your prior consent to change your apartment, and the prior written consent of at least two-thirds of allottees to change the building or common areas. Only limited minor changes are exempt. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [What happens to my flat if the builder goes insolvent?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/builder-insolvency-homebuyer-rights/): If the builder is a company or LLP, the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code treats the money you paid as financial debt, which makes you a financial creditor. Buyers in the same project can start insolvency together, vote through an authorised representative, and share in any resolution plan. Pending cases against the builder pause during the moratorium. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [Can a builder in Bengaluru charge separately for car parking?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/can-builder-sell-car-parking-separately/): The RERA Act treats "open parking areas" as common areas, which belong to all allottees. A "garage", meaning a roofed space walled on three sides, is defined separately and can be a distinct item. Whether a covered stilt or basement slot counts as one turns on its physical form and your agreement. Ask what you're paying for. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [Can I cancel a flat booking and get my money back under RERA?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/cancel-flat-booking-refund-rera/): It depends who cancelled and why. If the builder misses the agreement handover date, section 18 lets you withdraw for a refund with prescribed interest, or stay and claim delay interest. If you cancel for your own reasons, the Act gives no general exit right; your agreement and booking terms control deductions. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [Carpet area vs super built-up area: what does RERA say a flat is?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/carpet-area-vs-super-built-up-rera/): Under the RERA Act, carpet area is the flat's net usable floor area, including internal walls. It excludes external walls, service shafts, exclusive balconies and exclusive terraces. "Super built-up area" isn't defined in the Act at all. It's a sales figure that loads a share of lobbies, lifts and clubhouse onto your flat. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [What should I check in the builder&#x27;s sale agreement before signing?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/check-builder-sale-agreement-before-signing/): Compare the draft with the proforma agreement uploaded on the project's Karnataka RERA page, then check carpet area, total price and what it includes, the payment schedule, the possession date, interest on delay (both ways), how changes to plans are handled, defect liability, cancellation terms and any extra charges. Have your own lawyer review it. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [When must the builder register the conveyance deed in my name?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/conveyance-deed-timeline-rera/): Section 17(1) of the RERA Act requires the builder to execute a registered conveyance deed in your favour within the period set by local law. Where there's no local law on it, the deed must be executed within three months of the occupancy certificate. Until conveyance, the builder remains responsible for its obligations under section 11(4). (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [Corpus fund vs maintenance deposit: what am I paying for and who holds it?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/corpus-fund-vs-maintenance-deposit/): A corpus (or sinking) fund is usually a long-horizon reserve for major repairs and replacements. A maintenance deposit or advance funds day-to-day operations. Until the association takes over, the promoter often holds both. RERA sections 11 and 17 push formation of the association and handover of common areas and documents. Get a written account of unspent balances. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [Are floor-rise and preferential location charges allowed under RERA?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/floor-rise-charges-rera/): RERA does not ban floor-rise or preferential location charges (PLC) by name. It does require a written agreement with a price based on carpet area and a full breakup. A premium you saw and signed for is normal. One that appears after booking is the real problem, so read every PLC line before paying a token. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [What hidden costs should I expect beyond the base price (GST, parking, PLC, maintenance, registration)?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/hidden-costs-flat-bangalore-beyond-base-price/): On top of the base price, a Bangalore flat usually carries some mix of floor rise and location charges, parking, clubhouse fees, GST on under-construction units, stamp duty and registration, utility deposits, advance maintenance, a corpus fund and legal fees. Amounts vary by project, so insist on a fully filled cost sheet and read it line by line. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [Can a builder raise the price after booking?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/price-escalation-clause-legal/): Not freely, once you have a registered agreement for sale. Karnataka RERA's proforma agreement calls the total price escalation-free, except for new or higher charges imposed by a competent authority, tax changes and a carpet-area recalculation after the occupancy certificate. Your own signed agreement decides, so read its price clauses before paying more than the booking amount. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [What is RERA&#x27;s 70% rule for project money, and how do I check it?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/project-bank-account-70-percent-rule/): Under section 4(2)(l)(D) of the RERA Act, a builder must deposit 70% of the money collected from buyers for a project in a separate account at a scheduled bank, use it only for that project's construction and land cost, and withdraw it in proportion to completion, certified by an engineer, an architect and a chartered accountant. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [The flat is smaller than the agreement says. What are my options?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/rera-carpet-area-mismatch-on-possession/): Measure the flat the way RERA defines carpet area and compare it with your agreement for sale and the RERA project page. If it is really smaller, put the gap to the builder in writing before you sign the possession letter. If they won't fix it, complain to Karnataka RERA; compensation claims go to its adjudicating officer. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [Does Karnataka RERA have a model agreement for sale, and must builders use it?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/rera-model-agreement-karnataka/): Yes. Section 13(2) of the RERA Act says the agreement for sale must be in the form the state prescribes, and Karnataka RERA publishes a Proforma Agreement of Sale. Builders file their version with the project's registration and must highlight every change. Compare your draft with the proforma before signing. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [Are subvention (no-EMI-till-possession) schemes safe?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/subvention-scheme-risks/): They can work, but the loan is still in your name. If the builder stops paying the pre-EMI it promised, the bank looks to you, and RBI warns your credit score can suffer. RBI also says bank disbursal must follow construction stages, not go upfront. Read the tripartite agreement and plan for the builder missing payments. (Author: Nitin Gupta)

## Home Loans, Taxes & Financial Structuring

- [When does a home loan balance transfer make sense?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/balance-transfer-home-loan/): A home loan balance transfer makes sense when the interest you save over the remaining tenure clearly beats every cost of switching, such as the new lender's processing, legal, valuation and documentation charges. For floating-rate home loans to individuals sanctioned or renewed from 1 January 2026, RBI bars lenders from charging a pre-payment fee. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [Why do home loans get rejected, and how do I check before applying?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/cibil-score-home-loan-rejection/): A home loan can fail on you, on the property, or on paperwork. RBI's Fair Practices Code says a lender must give you the main reasons for a rejection in writing. Before you apply, pull your free annual credit report, fix any errors, and check that the project's approvals are in place. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [Delayed project, EMIs running: who bears the interest?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/emi-during-construction-delay-who-pays/): Your bank loan and your builder agreement are two separate contracts. Delay interest under RERA section 18 is what the promoter owes you if possession misses the agreement date. Pre-EMI or EMI you already owe the bank still follows the loan documents unless the bank agrees otherwise in writing. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [Should I prepay my home loan or invest the surplus?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/emi-vs-prepayment-strategy/): Prepaying gives a certain return equal to your loan's interest rate, after any tax benefit you lose, while investing gives an uncertain one. Keep an emergency fund first, then compare. On floating-rate home loans sanctioned or renewed from 1 January 2026, RBI bars banks and lenders from charging individuals for prepaying. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [Fee-only advisor vs commission-based consultant: which model suits me?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/fee-only-vs-commission-real-estate-advisor/): A fee-only adviser is paid only by you, so they have no stake in which property you choose. A commission-based consultant is paid when a deal happens, usually by the developer on new projects, sometimes by you on resale, so there's a pull towards closing and towards partner projects. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [How much flat can I afford on my salary in Bengaluru?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/first-flat-budget-emi-to-income/): How much home loan can I get on salary? Banks start from take-home pay. SBI allows EMIs of 20% to 70% of net income, depending on slab, and the RBI says banks typically count 55–60% of disposable income. Existing EMIs come off first. Then the LTV cap and your cash for the down payment and charges set the flat price. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [My home loan is sanctioned. Why hasn&#x27;t the money been disbursed?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/home-loan-sanction-vs-disbursement/): A sanction is the bank's offer on stated terms; disbursement is the actual release of money, and RBI rules tie it to conditions. For under-construction flats, disbursal must follow construction stages, and money can wait for project clearances. Read every condition in your sanction letter and match it to the builder's demand. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [What home loan tax deductions remain under the Income-tax Act, 2025?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/home-loan-tax-benefit-new-act-2025/): Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, the home loan tax benefit survives with new section numbers. In the old regime you can claim up to ₹2 lakh of interest on a self-occupied home (section 22) and up to ₹1.5 lakh of principal, stamp duty and registration (section 123, shared). In the default new regime, the self-occupied interest deduction isn't available. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [How does a home loan for an under-construction flat work (tranches and pre-EMI)?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/home-loan-under-construction-flat-disbursement/): Banks usually sanction a loan against an approved under-construction project, then release money in stages tied to construction progress and your payment plan. Until full disbursement, you typically pay interest on the amount already released (often called pre-EMI). Loan-to-value, rates and stage lists vary by bank, so confirm them in your sanction letter. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [Will banks give a home loan on a Hoskote panchayat or municipal flat?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/hoskote-flat-loan-panchayat/): Yes, banks can give a home loan on Hoskote apartments for sale when the papers are complete: an approved plan, an occupancy certificate for a ready flat, clear title and a regular municipal or panchayat record. The risk is the record type. A taxed but unauthorised property has no approval, so lenders may refuse. Ask first. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [Joint home loan with your spouse: how do co-ownership and tax deductions work?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/joint-home-loan-co-owner-rules/): The joint home loan tax benefit works per person. Under section 24 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, each co-owner with a defined share is taxed separately and gets the self-occupied relief individually. So in the old regime, each spouse who owns a share and pays the EMI can claim up to ₹2 lakh of interest and ₹1.5 lakh of principal. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [Can NRIs pay for a Bengaluru flat from NRE or NRO, and take the money back later?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/nri-nre-nro-payment-repatriation/): Yes to both, with conditions. RBI lets NRIs and OCIs pay through banking channels, by inward remittance or from NRE, FCNR(B) or NRO accounts, but not with traveller's cheques or foreign currency notes. When you sell, your bank can let the proceeds go abroad if you paid in foreign exchange or from NRE/FCNR(B), for up to two residential properties. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [How much of a flat's sale proceeds can an NRI repatriate?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/nri-repatriation-sale-proceeds/): Under the RBI's NRI repatriation property sale rules, you can send abroad, on the property route, up to what you originally paid in foreign exchange, for no more than two homes. The rest goes into your NRO account and can be remitted up to USD 1 million per financial year, after tax. Your purchase records decide the split. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [What TDS applies when an NRI buys or sells a flat in Bangalore?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/nri-tds-buy-sell-property-india/): It depends on the seller, not the buyer. Buying from a resident seller, an NRI deducts 1% under Section 393(1) of the Income-tax Act, 2025, once the price or stamp duty value reaches ₹50 lakh. Buying from a non-resident seller falls under Section 393(2), at rates in force on the taxable sum. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [When does property tax start on a new flat in Bengaluru, and who pays it?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/property-tax-new-flat-bengaluru/): Inside Bengaluru corporation limits, tax on a constructed building is usually linked to lawful occupancy, often marked by the occupancy certificate, not by booking day. After conveyance, the khatadar or person primarily liable pays on the official property-tax portal. Confirm your PID and demand there, not via a broker forward. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [How is property tax paid for a flat under a gram panchayat (around Varthur, Hoskote, Budigere)?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/property-tax-panchayat-flat-east-bengaluru/): If your flat sits in a gram panchayat, common in the outer belts around Varthur, Hoskote and Budigere, you generally skip the BBMP corporation tax portal. Get the panchayat property ID from e-Swathu or e-khata, then pay via BSK, SAMARTH where enabled, or the panchayat office. Confirm jurisdiction first. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [How much down payment do I need? RBI&#x27;s loan-to-value limits explained](https://answers.acrenkey.com/rbi-ltv-down-payment-rules/): RBI caps how much of a home's value a bank can lend. For loans up to ₹30 lakh the cap is 90%, above ₹30 lakh up to ₹75 lakh it is 80%, and above ₹75 lakh it is 75%. You pay the rest yourself, plus stamp duty and registration, which banks can't count in the property's value. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [How does a home loan for a resale flat differ from a new flat?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/resale-flat-home-loan-process/): A resale flat is already built and owned by someone else, so there are no construction stages to pay against. The bank's checks move to the seller and the building: title, the sanctioned plan and completion certificate, any loan the seller still owes, and a valuation. RBI's rules let banks finance an old house. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [How does TDS on property purchase work from 1 April 2026?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/tds-on-flat-purchase-section-393-form-141/): For payments made on or after 1 April 2026, a buyer deducts TDS on a property purchase under Section 393(1), Table serial 3(i), of the Income-tax Act, 2025. The rate is 1% of the price or the stamp duty value, whichever is higher, once either reaches ₹50 lakh. The buyer reports it on Form 141, Schedule B. (Author: Nitin Gupta)

## Title, Approvals & Municipal Records (BBMP/Kaveri)

- [How do you transfer BESCOM and BWSSB connections to your name after a resale?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/bescom-bwssb-name-transfer-resale/): For BESCOM name change online inside GBA, finish your e-Khata mutation first. BESCOM then texts you a link. You log in, check the details pulled from GBA, pay ₹100, e-sign the indemnity bond for ₹1,194 and authenticate with Aadhaar. For water, apply on BWSSB's transfer portal for ₹250. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [When does a new flat get a permanent BESCOM connection?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/bescom-permanent-power-new-flat/): Permanent BESCOM supply is a separate service from temporary construction power. Temporary supply is surrendered before a permanent installation is arranged. After the permanent installation is serviced, BESCOM assigns an R.R. number painted on the meter board. Exact connection charges sit on the BESCOM subdivision demand letter, not on third-party tables. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [What civic body and water supply apply to Budigere Cross apartments?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/budigere-cross-water-and-civic-status/): Most Budigere Cross apartments sit under gram panchayats in Bengaluru East taluk, not a city corporation. Records live on e-Swathu, stamp charges total 7.65% rather than 7.6%, and the area isn't on Cauvery Stage 5. So Budigere Cross water supply usually means borewells and tankers unless a project can show a piped source in writing. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [How does a new apartment get a BWSSB water connection, and what does it cost buyers?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/bwssb-connection-new-apartment/): New apartment BWSSB connections usually go through the Board's online service: register, buy the application, upload papers, use a BWSSB-registered plumber, await inspection, then pay the official demand note. The exact charges sit on that note, not on blog tables. Ask whether the promoter already holds a bulk connection. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [How do I check whether an East Bangalore project falls under BBMP or a gram panchayat?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/check-bbmp-or-panchayat-east-bangalore/): Check who issues the khata and collects property tax on the project land, and who sanctioned the building plan. A khata from the city corporation (the former BBMP area, now Greater Bengaluru Authority) through e-Aasthi means a city property; one from a gram panchayat through e-Swathu means panchayat. Confirm it from documents on the project's Karnataka RERA page. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [How do you search a property on e-Aasthi by PID?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/e-aasthi-search-property-pid/): For an e aasthi search property by PID number, open GBA's e-Aasthi 2.0 portal, choose Search Property, and enter the 10-digit Property ePID. You can also search by ward or by SAS property tax ID. Searching is free; downloading a Final e-Khata costs ₹125, paid online. If it isn't listed, try partial names and the assessment number. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [What is Karnataka&#x27;s digital e-stamp and how do I pay stamp duty online?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/e-stamp-digital-karnataka-flat/): Karnataka's Digital e-Stamp is a government-issued electronic stamp generated after you pay stamp duty through the notified Digital e-Stamp application, typically reached via Kaveri Online Services. You register, enter instrument details, pay online, and receive a unique-numbered stamp stored in the official repository. Confirm live menus on the portal; do not trust third-party "stamp paper" sellers. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [What is e-Swathu, and how do you check a panchayat-area flat's record?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/e-swathu-property-records-flat/): e-Swathu is Karnataka's system for gram panchayat property records. For an e swathu property search, pick Form-9 or Form-11B, then search by property ID or by survey number with district, block, panchayat and village. Then verify the certificate number and use the portal's check on whether the property can be registered. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [How do you download an EC online from Kaveri 2.0?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/encumbrance-certificate-online-kaveri-steps/): The EC online Kaveri 2.0 route is simple: log in at kaveri.karnataka.gov.in, start an Encumbrance Certificate application, enter the district, office area, every property identifier and the search period, e-sign with Aadhaar, pay online, and download the digitally signed EC. Fees are ₹10 plus ₹30 for the first year and ₹10 per extra year. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [What should I check before taking possession of a new flat in Bengaluru?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/flat-possession-inspection-checklist/): Before you take keys, walk the flat room by room, match carpet area to your agreement, photograph defects, and collect the possession letter, occupancy certificate status, keys, meter readings and NOCs. Under RERA, structural and workmanship defects reported within five years of handover must be fixed free within 30 days. Do not skip a written snag list. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [Form 11A vs Form 11B in panchayat areas: what's the difference?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/form-11a-11b-panchayat-khata/): Form 11A vs 11B comes down to legality. Form 11A is the gram panchayat's e-Swathu record for regular, authorised property. Form 11B records property the panchayat taxes under section 199C: unconverted land, unapproved layouts or buildings without approvals. The law says paying 11B tax gives no regularisation, title, ownership or legal status. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [Can I start interiors in my new flat before possession or the OC?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/interiors-before-possession-rules/): Not as of right. Under RERA, the builder offers possession after getting the occupancy certificate, and you take it within two months. Early access for interiors before that is only by the builder's written permission. Even after possession, the model agreement bars structural changes, removing walls and altering the exterior of the building. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [How do I register a flat on Kaveri 2.0, step by step?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/kaveri-2-property-registration-steps/): Karnataka property registration runs through the Department of Stamps and Registration and its Kaveri online services. You typically prepare the deed with your lawyer, pay stamp duty and registration fees as assessed, book a slot, and complete biometrics at the sub-registrar. Kaveri 2.0 screen labels change, so follow the live portal rather than an old screenshot. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [What lift and generator documents should our association get at handover?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/lift-and-dg-maintenance-amc-handover/): RERA doesn't list equipment papers by name. Section 2(n) counts lifts, central electricity and water installations, pumps and motors as common areas, and section 17(2) makes the builder hand over the necessary documents and plans, including common areas, to the association. In practice, collect each machine's approvals, warranties, service contracts and service history. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [How do you get the khata transferred (mutation) after buying a flat?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/mutation-after-buying-flat-bengaluru/): Khata transfer after purchase means getting the city or panchayat record changed to your name. Inside GBA, it runs on e-Aasthi 2.0, which is linked to Kaveri registration. In panchayat areas, it's done on e-Swathu through the gram panchayat. Budget a mutation charge of 2% of the stamp duty you paid, minimum ₹500. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [What are OC and CC, and why do they matter when buying in Bangalore?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/oc-cc-importance-bangalore/): CC can mean two things: a commencement certificate, permission to start construction, or a completion certificate, confirmation that the building was completed as per the approved plans. OC is the occupancy certificate, permission to occupy the building. For a ready flat, the OC is the key document. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [The builder gave possession without an OC. What now?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/oc-not-received-after-possession/): Under RERA, obtaining the occupancy certificate (or completion certificate under local law) is the promoter's duty, and conveyance timelines are tied to it. Taking keys without an OC does not wipe those duties. Ask for the OC in writing, check the Karnataka RERA project page, and if needed file under section 31 with your lawyer. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [Does a possession letter replace the occupancy certificate?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/possession-letter-vs-oc/): No. A possession letter is the builder's own letter offering you the flat. The occupancy certificate (OC) is issued by the competent authority and permits people to occupy the building. Under the RERA Act, the builder must obtain the OC and make it available to you, and your two months to take possession run from the OC. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [How do you check the RTC (pahani) on Bhoomi for land under a project?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/rtc-pahani-check-bhoomi/): The RTC check online Karnataka offers runs on the Bhoomi portal. Select district, taluk, hobli, village, survey number, surnoc, hissa and year to see the record of rights. Check the owner, the extent, any kharab land and the mutation entries, then match the total extent with the land area the project declared on RERA. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [Builder still running maintenance after possession: what can owners do?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/rwa-maintenance-dispute-builder/): Under RERA section 11(4)(d), the builder must provide and maintain essential services on reasonable charges until the association of allottees takes over maintenance. Section 17 makes it hand over the common areas and documents to the association. If that hasn't happened, owners should form or activate the association, ask for handover in writing, and complain under section 31. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [Can an apartment association go solar under BESCOM net metering?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/solar-rooftop-apartment-bescom/): Yes. A solar rooftop apartment plant can run on the association's common-area connection under net metering, or share credits with residents under virtual net metering, which KERC's 2026 regulations allow for apartments. Size it to the common-area load, apply on BESCOM's portal after registering on PM Surya Ghar, and claim ₹18,000 per kW in subsidy. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [How do you check an apartment's STP and borewell compliance?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/stp-and-borewell-checks-apartment/): To check the STP in apartments you're considering, confirm whether the law requires one, then ask for the KSPCB Consent for Establishment and a current Consent for Operation, recent treated-water test reports and the plant's capacity. For borewells, ask for BWSSB or KGWA permission, summer yield and a water quality report. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [What can I do about defects after possession? The builder defect liability period under RERA](https://answers.acrenkey.com/structural-defects-after-possession-rera/): A defect in structure, workmanship, quality or services that you report within five years of possession must, under Section 14(3) of the RERA Act, be fixed by the builder free of charge within thirty days. If the builder fails, you're entitled to compensation. The duty continues even after conveyance deeds are executed. (Author: Arvind Patidar)

## East Bengaluru Micro-markets & Site Evaluation

- [Should I worry about buying near Bellandur or Varthur lake?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/bellandur-varthur-lake-living-near/): Buying near Bellandur lake or Varthur lake is worth a closer look, not a flat no. Both lakes are over 100 acres, so the full 30 m buffer still applies after the 2026 law change. The bigger risk is low ground: in 2022 the overflowing lakes flooded the land between them. Check the plot's level, buffer and flood history. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [Flood risk on Sarjapur Road and the ORR: how do I check a flat before buying?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/flood-risk-check-east-bengaluru-flat/): Sarjapur Road flooding is patchy, so check the flat, not the area. On Sarjapur Road or the outer ring road, look at four things: flood spots on the approach road, the distance to the nearest drain or lake, how high the basement ramp sits above the road, and what residents saw last monsoon. (Author: Arvind Patidar)
- [Buying near KR Puram or Old Madras Road: what's specific to check?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/kr-puram-old-madras-road-flat-checklist/): Buying a flat in KR Puram or along Old Madras Road comes with four corridor-specific checks: whether the address is inside the city or in a panchayat further east, your real walk to a running metro station, flood points that have filled with very little rain, and whether the guidance value is higher than your price, which raises your charges. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [Living along the ORR: what do noise and air quality data say before you buy?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/marathahalli-bellandur-flat-noise-air/): If you're comparing Bellandur flats for sale on the outer ring road, test noise and air for the specific flat. The legal residential noise limit is 55 dB(A) by day and 45 at night. The nearest official air monitor, at Kadabesanahalli, averaged about 37 µg/m³ of PM2.5 in one 2019–20 study, near the 40 annual limit. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [Panathur Road access and traffic: what should flat buyers know?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/panathur-railway-underpass-access/): Panathur Main Road traffic is the main thing to test before buying in Panathur, Balagere, Gunjur or Varthur. The railway underpass was widened to two vents in November 2025, but the S-Cross junction stayed a bottleneck and the underpass flooded four times between June and October 2026, per news reports. Drive it at peak hour and after rain. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [Which property consultant can help me buy near Marathahalli or Bellandur?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/property-consultant-marathahalli-bellandur/): Look for a property consultant who works the Outer Ring Road stretch from Marathahalli to Bellandur every week, not just someone with an office nearby. They should know which pockets are walkable to your office, which side roads choke at peak hour and which towers are occupied, and should show a valid Karnataka RERA agent registration. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [Who is the best property consultant in Whitefield for buying a flat?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/property-consultant-whitefield/): There's no neutral "best" list, and whoever hands you one is usually selling. For you, the best Whitefield consultant knows the exact pockets you're considering, shows a valid Karnataka RERA agent registration, says plainly who pays them, and will talk you out of a project. Judge every name this way, ours included. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [Which real estate consultants cover KR Puram and Old Madras Road?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/real-estate-consultant-kr-puram-old-madras-road/): Several consultants cover this belt. The useful question is who actually knows this belt. Old Madras Road changes a lot between KR Puram and Hoskote, so look for someone who can explain each stretch, check whether a project sits under the city corporation or a gram panchayat, verify RERA registration and say who pays them. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [Is there a good real estate consultant near Sarjapur Road for new launches?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/real-estate-consultant-sarjapur-road/): Yes, but on Sarjapur Road a consultant is only useful for new launches if they slow you down at the right moments. Good ones confirm the launch is on the Karnataka RERA portal before you pay anything, explain what an EOI commits you to, say who pays them, and know Sarjapur Road near Wipro from Sarjapur Road past Dommasandra. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [How should school commutes shape where you buy in East Bengaluru?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/school-commute-east-bengaluru-flat/): Pick the school first, then the flat. Families comparing schools near Whitefield often find the school run matters more than their own commute, because a child does it for a decade. Time both trips at peak, count the years left in school, and avoid routes that cross the ORR or a railway underpass that floods. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [Buying a 10–15-year-old apartment in Whitefield: what wears out?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/whitefield-older-apartment-resale-age/): In a 10–15-year-old resale flat in Whitefield, the things that wear out are mostly shared: lifts, terrace and bathroom waterproofing, plumbing risers, pumps, the generator and the STP. The builder's five-year defect liability under RERA is long over, so repairs fall on owners. Ask for the lift register, the repair history and the sinking fund balance. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [Whitefield or Sarjapur Road: which is better for a family buying their first flat?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/whitefield-vs-sarjapur-road-family-flat/): Neither wins outright. Whitefield tends to suit families who want an established neighbourhood, existing metro access and plenty of ready-to-move stock. Sarjapur Road tends to suit families willing to trade a less certain commute for newer projects and, further out, more space for the money. Start from where the earning parent works. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)

## Property Advisory & Consulting Services

- [Is a buyer-side real estate consultancy better than a developer-paid one?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/buyer-side-vs-developer-paid-consultancy/): A buyer-side real estate consultancy firm, one that you pay, has fewer conflicts on which project you choose. A developer-paid one costs you nothing directly but is pulled towards projects that pay it. Neither is better for everyone. If you want no seller money involved and are happy to pay, buyer-side makes sense. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [Can a consultant guarantee price appreciation or returns?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/can-consultant-guarantee-returns/): No. A consultant can't guarantee that a flat will rise in value or earn a fixed rent, because neither depends on them. Section 10 of the RERA Act bars registered agents from misleading representations. Treat any "assured return" or "buyback" as a contract term: get it in writing from whoever promises it, and have your lawyer read it. (Author: Nitin Gupta)
- [How do I choose a real estate consultancy firm in Bangalore?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/choose-real-estate-consultancy-firm-bangalore/): Score each real estate consultancy firm on six things: valid Karnataka RERA agent registration, who you'll actually work with, how well they know your target area, how clearly they disclose who pays them, how thorough their document checks are, and what they do after you book. Talk to at least two firms and compare. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [Real estate consultant vs broker vs advisory firm: which should a Bangalore buyer use?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/consultant-vs-broker-vs-advisory-bangalore/): Use a broker when you mainly need listings and someone to close. Use a consultant, usually developer-paid, for help shortlisting and checking new projects. Use a fee-paid advisory firm when you want someone paid only by you. The labels overlap a lot in Bangalore, so judge people by who pays them and what they'll do. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [Does a consultant replace your own property lawyer for title verification?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/consultant-vs-property-lawyer-title-check/): No. A real estate consultancy firm can gather documents and spot obvious gaps, but a title opinion should come from your own property lawyer you appoint. The lawyer reads the ownership chain, checks for encumbrances and disputes, confirms land conversion and approvals are valid, and reviews the agreement. They work only for you. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [How do I find a reliable real estate consultant near me in East Bangalore?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/find-reliable-real-estate-consultant-near-me-bangalore/): In East Bangalore, a reliable real estate consultant near you is someone who works your corridor every week (Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, Varthur, Marathahalli), shows a Karnataka RERA agent registration you can verify, and tells you upfront whether developers pay them. A nearby office or map pin alone proves nothing. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [What should a first-time homebuyer in Bangalore expect from a property consultant?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/first-time-buyer-property-consultant-bangalore/): Expect a property consultant in Bangalore to help you turn a vague wish into a clear brief, shortlist projects that fit, explain the paperwork in plain language, check RERA registration and key documents, negotiate, and walk you through the loan and registration. Don't expect them to replace your lawyer, guarantee returns or make the decision for you. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [What does the home buying process look like with a real estate consultant in Bangalore?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/home-buying-process-with-consultant-bangalore/): With a real estate consultant in Bangalore, the process usually runs: brief, shortlist, site visits, document checks, negotiation, booking, agreement for sale, home loan, payments as the project progresses, sale deed registration, and handover with khata transfer. The consultant coordinates and checks. You still make the decisions, sign the documents and use your own lawyer for title. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [How do property consultants in Bangalore get paid, by the buyer or the developer?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/how-property-consultants-bangalore-get-paid/): On primary sales, most property consultants in Bangalore are paid by the developer when a booking happens through them, not through a separate invoice to you. Buyers often pay no advisory fee at all. That doesn’t make the advice unbiased, so always ask who pays, and get the answer in writing. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [How do I choose a trustworthy real estate consultant in Bangalore?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/how-to-choose-real-estate-consultant-bangalore/): To choose a real estate consultant in Bangalore you can trust, verify their Karnataka RERA agent registration, ask who pays them, and see whether they’ll say “no” to a bad fit. Trustworthy consultants explain their fee arrangement in plain words and give you time to read documents before any token. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [What red flags suggest a property consultant in Bangalore may be running a scam?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/red-flags-real-estate-consultant-bangalore/): Stop if a consultant asks you to pay them personally instead of the developer, pushes a project that isn't on the Karnataka RERA portal, won't share their own RERA agent number, offers documents you can't verify, or promises guaranteed returns. Any one of these is reason enough. A genuine real estate consultant in Bangalore won't mind you checking. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [Should a real estate consultant disclose if a developer is paying them?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/should-consultant-disclose-developer-payment/): Yes. A consultant who may be paid by a developer when you book should say so plainly, before the first site visit and for each project they show you. The RERA Act has no specific commission-disclosure rule for agents, but it bars misleading claims about services, and you can't weigh advice without knowing who pays. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [How do I verify a property consultant&#x27;s RERA registration in Karnataka?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/verify-property-consultant-rera-karnataka/): Before you rely on any property consultant in Bangalore, get their Karnataka RERA agent registration number and check it yourself on rera.karnataka.gov.in (agent status search). The name, status and validity should all match, and you want this done before any token. (Author: Gaurav Mongia)
- [What are real estate consultancy services and what do they include?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/what-are-real-estate-consultancy-services/): For a homebuyer, real estate consultancy services cover the work between "I want a flat" and "I have the keys": setting your brief, shortlisting projects, site visits, RERA and paperwork checks, decoding cost sheets, booking and loan coordination, and follow-through to registration. Firms differ widely, so get the list in writing. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [What does a real estate consultant in Bangalore actually do for a homebuyer?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/what-does-real-estate-consultant-bangalore-do/): A real estate consultant in Bangalore turns your brief into a short list of suitable projects, filtering on location, budget, Karnataka RERA status, paperwork risk and timelines. They explain the trade-offs, arrange site visits and stay with you through booking and handover paperwork, without replacing your lawyer. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
- [What does a real estate investment consultant do?](https://answers.acrenkey.com/what-does-real-estate-investment-consultant-do/): An investment consultant helps you decide whether, where and what to buy as an investment rather than a home. For an individual in Bangalore, that usually means matching your goal (rental income, long-term growth, or both) to specific locations and projects, checking the risks, estimating costs and rents realistically, and planning how you'd eventually exit. (Author: Piyush Mittal)
